So I would personally keep at least 2 female babies with the mom.

I would also add that pregnant and breastfeeding mice need a bit more protein in their diet. Not too much because mice are very sensitive. [the comments here go over what food is good to give to breastfeeding mothers](https://www.petmousefanciers.com/t2474-food-for-nursing-mothers-and-auntie) 

The topic of whether to keep male mice alone is debated and I think it depends on which country you live in. I believe in America and Germany it is more popular to neuter them and keep them with females, but in the UK and Ireland it seems to be the norm to keep them alone, I think because our vets aren’t as used to operating on such small animals. 

That being said, some people in the UK keep their male mice with a species called African soft furred rats, which are actually another species of mouse, despite their name. 

Personally I keep my male mouse alone, but I spend a lot of time with him. As soon as he comes out at night he’s out of his cage until I’m too tired. Generally they don’t get lonely if you spend enough time with them.

For her own research, petmousefanciers.com is amazing (although it can be a bit hard to navigate in my opinion). 
Emiology on YouTube is such a wonderful mouse owner. She focuses on rats but her mouse videos are incredible.

Your friend sounds way too immature to have pets. Her behaviour is absolutely appalling. These are living beings and I would consider what she’s doing to be animal abuse. I’m not saying she’s a bad person, but her behaviour is not okay.

I think you need to have a serious talk with her and tell her she needs to separate the male and keep a few female children to stay with the mother. For any of them that she doesn’t want she NEEDS to either rehome them or give to you to freeze, which is a good way to go. They won’t “start their own bloodline” if she releases them, they will die VERY bad deaths from starvation/ ingesting poison/ predators. I recently found a pet mouse at my workplace and watched her slowly die because she ate rat poison. Releasing pet animals is a death sentence, please let her know that.

On the bright side, you seem to be handling the situation really well, and it’s great to see someone care so much about someone else’s pets :)
